audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls Void Shift a 'passive shield' and never states what it actually does: while he has not recently taken damage, Malzahar has massive damage reduction AND crowd-control immunity. That means Anivia's Flash Frost stun — the pivot of every line of advice here — simply does not apply to an untouched Malzahar.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'When he hasn't recently taken damage or been crowd controlled, Malzahar gains massive damage reduction and crowd control immunity.' Anivia's entire trade pattern is Q-stun into a chilled double-damage E. Opening with Q into a live Void Shift wastes the 11s cooldown for nothing, and no line on this page warns the reader.
audit.corrected: Chip him first — one Glacial Storm tick or an E strips Void Shift — and only then does the stun land. This is also what makes your Q able to cancel Nether Grasp's channel.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[2..4].side all read 'Skill' while win[2..4] read Malzahar, Malzahar, Anivia and packet.levelChart agrees with the content layer.
audit.why: The page renders two different answers to who wins Level 3, Levels 4-5 and Level 6. Content and packet agree with each other.
audit.corrected: phases[2].side = Malzahar, phases[3].side = Malzahar, phases[4].side = Anivia. Spikes: his are Call of the Void rank-ups (flat 6s) and Nether Grasp falling 140s to 80s; yours are Lost Chapter, Glacial Storm at 6, then Seraph's/RoA.

audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty advice tells you to bait his 'sidestep tool'; Malzahar has no dash, blink or movement ability at all.
audit.why: His kit is Q at 900 range, W at 150, E at 650 and a 700-range channel. What actually gates your step-up is the 6s silence and Void Shift, not mobility.
audit.corrected: Track the silence's 6s and the state of Void Shift; there is no dash to bait.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carries no numbers and describes Void Shift as a shield.
audit.why: Call of the Void is 6s flat, Malefic Visions 11s at rank 1, Nether Grasp 140s at rank 1 falling to 80s. Void Shift has no cooldown at all — it has a condition, which is a different kind of window and needs saying differently.
audit.corrected: Numbers written in, and Void Shift described as a condition you break rather than a timer you wait out.

audit.whatIsWrong: missingInteractions asserts 'Malzahar threatens a threshold kill with Malefic Visions (E) — track the HP number', driven by an 'execute' flag on his E.
audit.why: Riot's text describes no threshold: 'If the target dies while afflicted by the visions, they pass on to a nearby enemy unit and Malzahar gains Mana.' That is a spread-on-death effect, not an execute. Writing a threshold the reader then plays around would be a fabricated mechanic.
audit.corrected: The real effect worth knowing is the spread: Visions jumps to a nearby unit when its host dies, which is why one cast clears his wave and refunds his mana.

edits.before: Threaten Q until Malzahar burns his sidestep tool, land it, then E + auto and walk before the answer — chilled E double-damage is the whole trade.
edits.after: Break Void Shift first: one Glacial Storm tick or an E strips the damage reduction and CC immunity, and only then does your Flash Frost actually stun him.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Malzahar walks straight at you.
edits.after: Opening with Q into an untouched Void Shift — he is crowd-control immune until he takes damage, so the stun does not land at all.

edits.before: Good trade: Threaten Q until Malzahar burns his sidestep tool, land it, then E + auto and walk before the answer — chilled E double-damage is the whole trade. Bad trade: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Malzahar walks straight at you.
edits.after: Good trade: strip Void Shift with a storm tick or an E, then stun and E the chilled target for double damage — in that order, never the reverse. Bad trade: opening with Q into an untouched Void Shift, which is crowd-control immunity, so an 11-second cooldown buys you nothing and his 6-second silence answers whatever you have left.

edits.before: - Malzahar Nether Grasp: matchup-defining — Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Crystallize like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Void Shift: no cooldown, only a condition — the damage reduction and CC immunity drop once he takes a hit, so chip before you stun. - Call of the Void: 6s at 900 range, and the silence locks out your Q and your wall. - Nether Grasp: 140s at rank 1.

edits.before: - Anivia vs Malzahar - Track: Malzahar Nether Grasp. - Hold Q for his engage — never spend the stun on poke. - No commits into Nether Grasp. - The ultimate closes arguments; it doesn’t open them.
edits.after: - Anivia vs Malzahar - Track: Void Shift — chip him once, and only then does your stun land. - Call of the Void silences at 900 on a 6s cooldown. - Nether Grasp is a channel; your Q ends it.

edits.after: Void Shift gives him crowd-control immunity until he takes damage — strip it with a Glacial Storm tick before you ever spend Flash Frost on him.

edits.before: Threaten Q until Malzahar burns his sidestep tool, land it, then E + auto and walk before the answer — chilled E double-damage is the whole trade.
edits.after: Nether Grasp is a channel and 140 seconds at rank 1 — your stun ends it outright, provided you have already broken Void Shift with chip damage.

edits.before: Malzahar whiffs Nether Grasp and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Malzahar spends Nether Grasp and it is 140 seconds down at rank 1.

edits.before: That is Malzahar’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: That silence is only 6 seconds down and it locks out your wall as well as your stun.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Malzahar walks straight at you.
edits.after: Malefic Visions passes to a nearby unit when its host dies, so his wave clears itself while you chase a bar that keeps refreshing.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by breaking Void Shift before anything else: until he has taken damage, your stun and your storm slow both do nothing to him.

edits.before: Ahead, the lane is a prison: storm every wave, wall Malzahar away from the comeback farm, and rotate first to every river fight with your stun loaded.
edits.after: Ahead, deny the Visions economy: shove with R so his E never chains through a wave, and keep chip on him so Void Shift is never up when you commit.

edits.before: If Malzahar takes first blood, tighten up: Nether Grasp is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with R wave-clear and stay relevant through zone control.
edits.after: If Malzahar takes first blood, Nether Grasp starts converting — never stand inside 700 without the stun ready to end the channel. A second kill means farm with R wave-clear and break Void Shift before every single trade.

edits.after: Chip Void Shift off him before you ever spend Flash Frost's stun

edits.before: Malzahar's silence shuts down your engage tools and there's no clean counterplay yet

notes: packet.suspectNames flagged 'Use Crystallize' as a probable wrong ability name — FALSE POSITIVE, Crystallize is correct. The string was rewritten anyway for a different reason: 'escape silences' is not something Crystallize does, since a silence prevents casting it in the first place. Flag misfire recorded and deliberately not written: Malefic Visions carries an 'execute' flag and missingInteractions asks for an HP threshold, but Riot's text describes a spread-on-death, not an execute — no threshold claim was written. The biggest gap on the page is Void Shift: it is described as a 'passive shield' and its crowd-control immunity, which blanks Anivia's only stun, appears nowhere; that is now the spine of the rewritten trading, cooldown and carry text. Three-row level-chart fix proposed as one atomic group; the content layer already matched the packet.
